strengths: The manuscript clearly explains why interpretable macro-level features can be confounded with predictions even when the pixel-to-prediction mapping is deterministic. This distinction offers useful insight to researchers in causal explainability and model auditing. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-lrdv_216/call-2bdaa1ba6abb4979bbca034fd65bdc8b/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

PAG learning is an appropriate framework for representing latent confounding and unresolved causal directions under the stated assumptions. The background constraint that predictions cannot cause image contents is well motivated.

The synthetic example, two image applications, bootstrap analyses, and alternative discovery algorithm make the proposal concrete. The writing generally communicates the framework clearly, and the discussion acknowledges limitations involving faithfulness, feature selection, and annotation error.
weaknesses: Necessary: Correct the interpretation of feature relevance in Sections 6.3–6.4 and Figures 9–10. The ranking counts edges adjacent to the prediction, but a nonadjacent feature can still cause predictions through another observed feature. For example, Z1 → Z2 → prediction makes Z1 causally relevant despite its missing adjacency. Moreover, pooling directed and partially directed edges combines definite ancestry with cases compatible with confounding alone. Use ancestry-based reasoning or narrow the conclusions to adjacency, and report definite and possible causes separately.

Necessary: Repair Example 1 and Appendix A. The purported valid causal Shapley calculation leaves Z1 at its observational marginal when intervening on Z3, although the stated SCM contains Z3 → Z1. Consequently, those coalition values generally differ from the corresponding SCM interventional expectations. Appendix A.2 also retains the supposedly omitted z3 without defining an estimator available from the observed variables. Specify the coalition estimand and derive a valid comparison before treating this example as evidence of omitted-confounder bias.

Necessary: Address selection in the pneumonia experiment. The 120 controls are explicitly selected for having no findings, so inclusion depends on the explanatory findings as well as disease status. This requires justification against the earlier assertion that selection bias is irrelevant. Explain the sampling mechanism and target population, account for its implications, or restrict the clinical conclusions to exploratory associations under additional assumptions.

Necessary: Substantiate or narrow the empirical reliability claims. Conditional chi-square tests involving multilevel bird attributes and conditioning sets of size four can produce sparse contingency tables; the X-ray analysis contains only 240 images. Specify the observations used for discovery and provide evidence that the tests are appropriate for the resulting cell counts. Bootstrap stability and clinical plausibility do not independently validate causal conclusions. The change from Wing Shape/Wing Pattern under FCI to Crown Color/Size under GRaSP-FCI also warrants stronger qualification of the bird findings.

Optional: Repeated synthetic experiments with controlled feature interventions would help characterize finite-sample reliability. A comparison using the same macro-level annotations would better isolate the benefit of causal discovery from the benefit of supplying interpretable features; the selected LIME/SHAP visualizations primarily illustrate differences in explanatory granularity.
